claims.text: In refractory BCC high-entropy alloys, unusually high hardness and strength are governed predominantly by edge-dislocation-mediated plasticity.
Multi-principal-element interactions inherently produce lattice distortions and increased local misfit.
Increased local lattice misfit promotes the nucleation of edge dislocations.
Increased local lattice misfit promotes thermal super-jogging of edge dislocations.
Edge dislocations act as stronger barriers to plastic flow than conventional screw dislocations in these alloys.
NbTaTiV and CrMoNbV can represent single-phase refractory BCC HEAs having significant composition-induced lattice distortion.
Composition changes and controlled heat treatments can tune lattice misfit and related distortions.
The proposed mechanism should operate from room temperature through approximately 673–1073 K.
Plastic flow in conventional BCC elemental metals and dilute alloys is generally controlled by screw dislocations.
BCC HEAs engineered to have lower lattice misfit will exhibit predominantly screw-dislocation behavior.
Heterogeneous strain fields created by multi-element interactions destabilize the typical screw-dislocation core.
Heterogeneous strain fields facilitate edge-dislocation nucleation and thermal activation.
Thermal super-jogging gives edge dislocations higher lattice friction.
Edge-dislocation barriers impede plastic flow and thereby increase hardness and strength.
Alloys with enhanced lattice distortion will have a higher fraction of mobile edge dislocations than lower-misfit controls.
Alloys with enhanced lattice distortion will exhibit an elevated-temperature strength plateau.
Alloys with enhanced lattice distortion will have higher nanoindentation hardness than lower-misfit controls.
Alloys with enhanced lattice distortion will have higher yield strength than lower-misfit controls.
The mechanism is limited to compositionally complex refractory HEAs with a BCC structure and substantial lattice distortion.
The mechanism may not apply to FCC or dual-phase HEAs when twinning or interphase-boundary strengthening dominates.
